title: Do Multilingual Language Models Capture Differing Moral Norms?
benchmark_measurement: The paper measures how well multilingual language models capture and differentiate general moral norms and cultural values across different languages. It does not measure any aspects specifically related to faith or religion.
findings: The paper does not analyze or report any findings related to religion or faith. Its primary finding is that multilingual language models (specifically a tuned XLM-R) can capture moral norms, sometimes with higher human-agreement than monolingual models, but it is unclear to what extent these captured norms differ between languages.
